cashTip: Vietnamese dong cash is essential at stalls, boats and markets; check note denominations carefully.
name: Ha Long Bay
tagline: Thousands of limestone islands rising from an emerald sea
summary: Ha Long Bay's nearly 2,000 limestone pillars and islets make one of Asia's most famous seascapes. Most visitors sleep aboard a junk-style cruise boat, kayaking through lagoons, exploring caves and waking to mist over the karsts. Quieter Lan Ha and Bai Tu Long bays sit right next door.
seasonNote: March to May and October to November bring the clearest, calmest days. Summer is hot with storms that can cancel cruises. Winter is cool and often misty.
arrival: Most visitors come from Hanoi by limousine van or bus in about 2.5 hours on the expressway; many cruises include the transfer. Vietnam's e-visa covers most nationalities.
gettingAround: Cruises and day boats leave from Tuan Chau and Bai Chay harbours. Cat Ba Island links to Lan Ha Bay by boat.
foodTip: Fresh seafood, chả mực (squid cakes) and bánh cuốn rolls.
buyTip: Pearls are sold widely; buy only from reputable shops.
baseArea: On an overnight cruise, or Bai Chay or Cat Ba town

connections.note: Limousine vans and buses on the expressway.
Direct shuttles run between the two.

items.name: Overnight bay cruise
items.summary: A night aboard a wooden junk among the karsts, with kayaking, cave stops and a sunrise tai chi session.
items.expect: Prices vary hugely; read recent reviews on safety and food.
items.tip: Pick a route that avoids the busiest central loop.
items.why: The classic way to see the bay.

items.name: Sung Sot Cave
items.summary: 'Surprise Cave', the bay's biggest, with huge lit chambers of stalactites.
items.expect: Many steps and crowds at midday.
items.tip: Go early or late in the day.

items.name: Ti Top Island
items.summary: A small island with a sandy beach and a steep climb to a panoramic lookout.
items.why: The best view over the bay.

items.name: Lan Ha Bay kayaking
items.summary: Quieter karst bays with floating villages, lagoons and small beaches.
items.expect: Reached from Cat Ba or on Lan Ha cruises.
items.why: Ha Long's beauty with fewer boats.

items.name: Cat Ba National Park
items.summary: Forested hills with a hike to the Ngu Lam peak and home to the rare Cat Ba langur.
items.tip: Hike the short Ngu Lam summit trail.

items.name: Thien Cung Cave
items.summary: 'Heavenly Palace Cave', full of lit rock formations.
items.tip: Pair with nearby Dau Go Cave.

items.name: Bai Tu Long Bay
items.summary: The quieter northern bay, with the same limestone scenery and far fewer boats.
items.expect: Choose a cruise that goes there.
items.tip: Ideal for a calmer overnight cruise.

items.name: Chả mực squid cakes
items.summary: Pounded squid patties fried golden, the local speciality.
items.tip: Eat it with sticky rice or bánh cuốn.

items.name: Seafood restaurants
items.summary: Choose live crab, prawns and clams from tanks, cooked to order.
items.expect: Agree the price per kilo before cooking.

items.name: Bánh cuốn
items.summary: Silky steamed rice rolls, here often served with squid cake.

cashTip: Vietnamese dong cash is essential at stalls, boats and markets; check note denominations carefully.
name: Hue
tagline: Vietnam's imperial capital on the Perfume River
summary: Hue was the seat of the Nguyen emperors from 1802 to 1945. Its walled Imperial City, royal tombs set in pine-covered hills and riverside pagodas make it Vietnam's richest historic city, and its food is spicy and refined.
seasonNote: February to April is best. Summer is very hot. September to December is the rainy season, with floods some years.
arrival: Phu Bai Airport is 25 minutes from the centre with flights from Hanoi and Saigon. Trains and cars from Da Nang take about 2.5 hours.
gettingAround: Walk or cycle the centre. Take a taxi, Grab or motorbike tour to the tombs.
foodTip: Bún bò Huế, cơm hến and royal-style small cakes.
buyTip: Conical hats, sesame candy and Hue tea.
baseArea: South bank near Le Loi street

connections.note: Scenic coastal line over the Hai Van Pass.
Many drivers stop at the Hai Van Pass.

items.name: Imperial City
items.summary: The Nguyen emperors' walled palace city, with gates, throne halls and the Forbidden Purple City.
items.expect: Large site; much was damaged in 1968 and is being restored.
items.tip: Go late afternoon when evening openings run.

items.name: Thien Mu Pagoda
items.summary: A seven-storey pagoda on a bluff above the river, Hue's symbol.

items.name: Tomb of Khai Dinh
items.summary: A hillside tomb blending Vietnamese and European styles with dazzling mosaic rooms.
items.tip: See the glass and porcelain mosaics.

items.name: Tomb of Tu Duc
items.summary: A lake, pavilions and pine trees built as a retreat for a poet emperor.
items.tip: Combine with Khai Dinh and Minh Mang.

items.name: Tomb of Minh Mang
items.summary: A grand, symmetrical tomb complex set among lakes.

items.name: Perfume River dragon boat
items.summary: A slow boat along the river to Thien Mu and back.
flow: Board by the Truong Tien bridge.

items.name: Dong Ba Market
items.summary: Hue's biggest market for food, hats and cloth.
items.tip: Try the street food stalls inside.

items.name: Hai Van Pass
items.summary: A mountain road with famous sea views, often ridden by motorbike.
items.expect: Easiest as a stop on the Hue to Hoi An drive.
items.tip: Ride it with an Easy Rider guide.

items.name: Bún bò Huế
items.summary: Spicy lemongrass beef noodle soup with pork knuckle.
items.tip: Add shrimp paste and chilli to taste.

items.name: Cơm hến
items.summary: Rice with tiny river clams, herbs, peanuts and crackling.
items.tip: Try it on Con Hen islet.

items.name: Bánh bèo and royal cakes
items.summary: Small steamed rice cakes topped with shrimp, plus other bite-sized imperial snacks.
items.tip: Order bánh bèo, nậm and lọc together.

items.name: Vegetarian (chay) restaurants
items.summary: Hue's Buddhist tradition means excellent vegetarian versions of local dishes.

cashTip: Vietnamese dong cash is essential at stalls, boats and markets; check note denominations carefully.
name: Ninh Binh
tagline: Ha Long Bay on land, with rice fields and river caves
summary: Around Ninh Binh, limestone peaks rise from rice paddies and rivers that flow through caves. Rowing boats carry visitors through Trang An and Tam Coc, while temples, an ancient capital and a hilltop viewpoint fill the rest of a stay.
seasonNote: Late May to early June brings golden rice in Tam Coc. Spring and autumn are mild. Summer is hot and wet; winter is cool and grey.
arrival: Trains and buses from Hanoi take about 2 to 2.5 hours. Many hotels arrange pickups.
gettingAround: Rent a bicycle or scooter, or hire a car; the sights are spread out.
foodTip: Mountain goat meat and crispy rice (cơm cháy).
buyTip: Embroidery from Van Lam village near Tam Coc.
baseArea: Tam Coc or Trang An homestays

connections.note: Several trains a day; buses take about 2 hours.

items.name: Trang An boat trip
items.summary: A rowing-boat trip through river caves, karst valleys and temples.
items.expect: About 2 to 3 hours; rowers are local villagers.
items.tip: Pick a route with the most caves.

items.name: Tam Coc
items.summary: A river through rice fields and three caves, rowed by locals using their feet.
items.expect: Best when the rice is golden in late May.

items.name: Mua Cave viewpoint
items.summary: About 500 steps up to a dragon statue with views over Tam Coc.
items.expect: Hot climb; go early or at sunset.

items.name: Hoa Lu ancient capital
items.summary: Temples of Vietnam's 10th-century capital among the limestone peaks.

items.name: Bai Dinh Pagoda
items.summary: A huge modern Buddhist complex with giant bronze statues and long galleries of arhats.
items.expect: Very large; electric carts run inside.

items.name: Cuc Phuong National Park
items.summary: Vietnam's oldest national park, with ancient trees and a primate rescue centre.
items.expect: A day trip; bring insect repellent.

items.name: Phat Diem Cathedral
items.summary: A 19th-century stone and wood cathedral built in a Vietnamese pagoda style.
items.tip: Look at the carved wooden columns.

items.name: Mountain goat
items.summary: Local goat grilled, steamed or as a salad with herbs.

items.name: Cơm cháy crispy rice
items.summary: Crunchy sheets of rice topped with a meat or seafood sauce.

items.name: Phở for breakfast
items.summary: Hot beef or chicken noodle soup at village stalls.

cashTip: Vietnamese dong cash is essential at stalls, boats and markets; check note denominations carefully.
name: Sapa
tagline: Rice terraces and hill-tribe villages in the far north
summary: Sapa is a mountain town near the Chinese border, surrounded by rice terraces carved into steep valleys. Hmong, Dao and other ethnic minority guides lead treks between villages, and a cable car climbs Fansipan, the highest peak in Indochina.
seasonNote: September has golden rice before harvest. Spring brings green terraces and flowers. Summer is rainy, and winter can be near freezing with fog.
arrival: Sleeper buses and limousine vans from Hanoi take about 5.5 hours on the expressway. Night trains go to Lao Cai, then it's an hour by road.
gettingAround: Walk the town; trek or ride a motorbike taxi to villages. Hire a local guide for treks.
foodTip: Salmon hotpot, bamboo-tube rice and grilled skewers.
buyTip: Hmong indigo textiles and embroidery, bought directly from makers.
baseArea: Sapa town, or a village homestay in Ta Van

connections.note: Sleeper buses and limousine vans; night trains go to Lao Cai.

items.name: Fansipan cable car
items.summary: A cable car up the 3,143 m 'Roof of Indochina', with temples near the summit.
items.expect: Cold at the top; often in cloud.
items.tip: Go early for the best chance of clear views.

items.name: Muong Hoa Valley trek
items.summary: A trek through rice terraces to Lao Chai and Ta Van villages.
items.expect: Muddy in the wet season; wear good shoes.

items.name: Cat Cat village
items.summary: A Black Hmong village with a waterfall, now very touristy but close to town.
items.tip: Go early before the tour groups.

items.name: O Quy Ho Pass
items.summary: One of Vietnam's great mountain passes, with views of the Hoang Lien range.
items.tip: Stop at Heaven's Gate at sunset.

items.name: Ham Rong Mountain
items.summary: A garden hill above town with orchids and views over the valley.

items.name: Stone Church and town square
items.summary: A French-era stone church at the heart of Sapa town.
items.expect: The square is lively at weekends.

items.name: Bac Ha Sunday market
items.summary: A colourful Sunday market where Flower Hmong come to trade buffalo, produce and cloth.
items.expect: Sunday mornings only; about 2.5 hours by road.

items.name: Salmon hotpot
items.summary: Hotpot with salmon and sturgeon farmed in cold mountain streams.

items.name: Cơm lam bamboo rice
items.summary: Sticky rice cooked over coals inside bamboo tubes.

items.name: Night grill stalls
items.summary: Skewers of pork, mushrooms, corn and eggs grilled over charcoal.
items.expect: Around the town square at night.

cashTip: Vietnamese dong cash is essential at stalls, boats and markets; check note denominations carefully.
name: Phu Quoc
tagline: Vietnam's tropical island of white sand and sunsets
summary: Phu Quoc is Vietnam's biggest island, off the south coast near Cambodia. It has white-sand beaches, coral reefs in the An Thoi islands, jungle in the north, fish sauce factories and a famous night market. Big resorts and a record-breaking cable car now share it with fishing villages.
seasonNote: November to April is dry and sunny. May to October brings monsoon rain and rougher seas on the west coast.
arrival: Phu Quoc Airport has flights from Saigon (1 hour) and Hanoi (2 hours). Many nationalities can visit the island visa-free for up to 30 days, but check current rules.
gettingAround: Rent a scooter or use Grab and taxis; the island is large.
foodTip: Fresh seafood, herring salad (gỏi cá trích) and bún quậy noodles.
buyTip: Fish sauce (sealed for flights), pepper and pearls.
baseArea: Long Beach near Duong Dong, or the south for quiet beaches

items.name: Sao Beach
items.summary: A curve of fine white sand and calm turquoise water.
items.expect: Busy with boat groups at midday.

items.name: Hon Thom cable car
items.summary: One of the world's longest sea-crossing cable cars, over fishing boats to Hon Thom island.
items.expect: Ticket includes the island's water park.
items.tip: Ride it in the morning light.

items.name: An Thoi islands snorkelling
items.summary: A boat trip around small southern islands with coral and fish.

items.name: Phu Quoc Prison
items.summary: A wartime prisoner camp museum with sobering displays.
items.tip: Allow time to read the panels.

items.name: Phu Quoc National Park
items.summary: Forested hills covering much of the northern island, with streams and wildlife.
items.expect: Go with a guide for hikes.
items.tip: Visit Da Ban stream in the wet season.

items.name: Fish sauce factory
items.summary: Wooden vats where anchovies ferment into the island's famous fish sauce.
items.tip: Buy a sealed bottle; airlines ban loose ones.

items.name: Dinh Cau rock temple and sunset
items.summary: A small temple on a rock at the harbour mouth, honoured by fishermen.
items.tip: Come for sunset, then walk to the night market.

items.name: Night market seafood
items.summary: Stalls grilling squid, scallops, sea urchin and crab every night.
items.tip: Try grilled scallops with scallion oil.

items.name: Herring salad
items.summary: Raw herring with coconut, herbs and peanuts, wrapped in rice paper.

items.name: Bún quậy
items.summary: Fresh noodles with shrimp and fish paste; you mix your own sauce.
items.expect: A famous local shop is often busy.

cashTip: Vietnamese dong cash is essential at stalls, boats and markets; check note denominations carefully.
name: Da Lat
tagline: A cool, pine-covered hill town of lakes and flowers
summary: Da Lat sits at 1,500 m in Vietnam's Central Highlands, with a spring-like climate the French loved. It's known for pine forests, waterfalls, flower farms, a quirky 'Crazy House', coffee and a lively night market. Vietnamese couples come for honeymoons, and backpackers for canyoning.
seasonNote: December to March is dry and sunny. The Flower Festival is held in December in some years. May to October brings afternoon rain.
arrival: Lien Khuong Airport is 40 minutes away with flights from Saigon and Hanoi. Buses from Saigon take 7 to 8 hours.
gettingAround: Walk the centre; use Grab, taxis or a rented scooter for sights outside town.
foodTip: Bánh tráng nướng ('Vietnamese pizza'), bánh căn, hot soy milk and local coffee.
buyTip: Artichoke tea, strawberry jam, coffee and dried fruit.
baseArea: Around Xuan Huong Lake and the market

items.name: Crazy House
items.summary: A fairy-tale building of twisting tunnels, bridges and tree-like towers.
items.expect: Narrow walkways; it can be busy.

items.name: Xuan Huong Lake
items.summary: A crescent lake at the town's heart with walking paths and swan boats.

items.name: Da Lat railway station
items.summary: A 1930s Art Deco station with a short tourist train to Trai Mat.

items.name: Linh Phuoc Pagoda
items.summary: A pagoda covered in broken-glass and porcelain mosaics, with a giant dragon.

items.name: Datanla Falls
items.summary: Waterfalls in pine forest with a mountain coaster ride down.

items.name: Canyoning
items.summary: Abseiling down waterfalls and jumping into pools with a guide.

items.name: Langbiang Mountain
items.summary: A peak above flower valleys, hiked or reached by jeep.
items.tip: Hike to the top for big views.

items.name: Truc Lam Monastery and cable car
items.summary: A Zen monastery above Tuyen Lam Lake, reached by cable car over pine forest.

items.name: Bánh tráng nướng
items.summary: Rice paper grilled over coals with egg, scallion and toppings.

items.name: Bánh căn
items.summary: Little rice cakes cooked in clay moulds, dipped in fish sauce.

items.name: Coffee and hot soy milk
items.summary: Coffee grown in the highlands, and warm soy milk at night stalls.
items.tip: Try egg coffee or a pour-over.

cashTip: Carry some yuan as backup; mobile payment is common but foreign setup and acceptance can vary.
name: Xi'an
tagline: The Terracotta Army and the start of the Silk Road
summary: Xi'an was China's capital for over a thousand years and the eastern end of the Silk Road. Outside the city stands the Terracotta Army, thousands of life-size clay soldiers. Inside, you can cycle the Ming city walls, visit the Great Mosque and eat through the Muslim Quarter.
seasonNote: Spring and autumn are best. Summer is hot and busy. Avoid the October Golden Week and Chinese New Year crowds.
arrival: Xianyang Airport is about an hour from the centre. High-speed trains reach Beijing in about 4.5 hours. Check current visa and visa-free transit rules.
gettingAround: Metro lines cross the city. Bus 306 or a tour goes to the Terracotta Army.
foodTip: Roujiamo, biangbiang noodles, yangrou paomo and liangpi cold noodles.
buyTip: Terracotta warrior replicas, shadow puppets and calligraphy.
baseArea: Inside the city walls near the Bell Tower

connections.note: Approximate flight time; trains take about 6 hours.

items.name: Terracotta Army
items.summary: Thousands of life-size clay warriors guarding the tomb of China's first emperor.
items.why: One of the world's great archaeological finds.

items.name: City walls by bike
items.summary: Cycle the 14 km loop on top of China's best-preserved city walls.

items.name: Great Mosque
items.summary: A 14th-century mosque built like a Chinese temple, with courtyards and pagoda minaret.
items.expect: Closed to non-Muslims at prayer times.

items.name: Giant Wild Goose Pagoda
items.summary: A Tang dynasty pagoda built to hold scriptures brought from India.
items.expect: Evening fountain shows on the north square.

items.name: Shaanxi History Museum
items.summary: One of China's finest museums, covering Zhou to Tang dynasties.
items.expect: Free tickets must be booked ahead.

items.name: Bell and Drum Towers
items.summary: Ming towers at the city's centre, with daily drum performances.
items.why: The heart of the old city.

items.name: Forest of Steles
items.summary: Over 3,000 stone tablets of calligraphy and history.

items.name: Mount Hua
items.summary: A sacred Taoist mountain of granite peaks, cable cars and dizzying cliff paths.
items.expect: A long day trip by fast train; very busy at weekends.
items.tip: Use the cable cars to save energy.
items.why: One of China's five great mountains.

items.name: Muslim Quarter food street
items.summary: Lanes of halal stalls selling lamb skewers, persimmon cakes and noodles.
items.tip: Try a little at many stalls.

items.name: Roujiamo
items.summary: The 'Chinese burger': slow-cooked beef or lamb in a crisp flatbread.
items.expect: Halal versions in the Muslim Quarter.

items.name: Yangrou paomo
items.summary: Lamb soup poured over flatbread you tear into small pieces yourself.
items.tip: Ask how fine to tear it.

items.name: Biangbiang noodles and liangpi
items.summary: Belt-wide hand-pulled noodles with chilli oil, and cold liangpi noodles.
